text: According to the Axiom of Extensionality, when are two sets A and B equal?
choices: When they have exactly the same elements
When they have the same number of elements
When one is a subset of the other
When they were constructed using the same axioms
explanation: Extensionality says A = B iff ∀x(x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ B) — a set's identity is fixed entirely by its members. Having the same number of elements is far weaker (e.g. {1} and {2}); one-way subset inclusion is not equality; and how a set was built is irrelevant to its identity.
